public_brief: Our design-system portal has a color field where designers paste hex swatches, and a backend gate decides on the spot whether a value may enter the brand palette. Implement is_valid_brand_color(color), which takes the value exactly as pasted and returns True when the toolkit would accept it and False when it would bounce it. The toolkit only speaks hex, it recognizes a specific set of notations, and a couple of tones are spoken for; the gate owns all of that. Keep it a pure function: no printing, no prompting, no filesystem or network access. Graders call it directly with ordinary swatches and with adversarial junk - odd lengths, weird casing, odd types - and compare return values, so every input path needs a defined answer.
entry_contract: Implement is_valid_brand_color(color) taking one positional argument of any type and returning a strict bool (True or False) for every input.

hidden_spec.rule: Exactly three notations are accepted: #RGB (three hex digits), #RRGGBB (six), and #RRGGBBAA (eight), always opening with '#'; the four-digit short-alpha form #RGBA, any other length, and a value with no leading hash are all invalid.
CSS-style color names such as 'red', 'aliceblue', or 'transparent' are rejected - the toolkit takes hex strings only.
Hex digits are case-insensitive: upper, lower, and mixed case within one value are all accepted.

Pure black #000000 and pure white #FFFFFF are reserved for the layout canvas and are never brand colors; they are rejected in any accepted notation, including the short forms #000 and #FFF and any alpha-suffixed spelling, while mid-grays such as #808080 are fine.
In the eight-digit form the alpha byte must be strictly between 00 and FF: 00 is invisible and FF is just the opaque six-digit color, so #RRGGBB00 and #RRGGBBFF are rejected.
Any non-string argument returns False and never raises; numeric RGB ints are not coerced.
The value is judged exactly as typed: leading or trailing whitespace is never trimmed and makes it False.

answer_sheet.answer: Three shapes ship from the toolkit: #RGB, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA. The short-with-alpha #RGBA never made it into the toolkit, and the picker always sends the hash - a bare hex string is a paste accident.
Hex only. The moment we allowed 'cornflowerblue' we had two sources of truth, so keywords bounce.
Case means nothing to us - FF, ff, and fF in the same value are all the same color. Designers paste from five different tools.
Pure black and pure white belong to the layout canvas - type and paper - so no brand swatch can use them in any spelling. Mid-grays are open season.
Alpha 00 is invisible and FF is just the six-digit color wearing a coat, so both are rejected at the door. Anything strictly between ships fine.
Anything that isn't text comes back False - we do not coerce the numeric RGB int somebody pastes from a JS console.
Judge it as typed. A padded value fails; the form field is supposed to have handled trimming before we ever see it.
Out of scope - WCAG contrast math happens in the theme checker, not the swatch gate.
Out of scope - no database, no lookup against saved swatches; this is a pure predicate on the string.

provenance.derivation: Rules derived from real brand-guideline and CSS hex-color conventions (#RGB/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA notations with the short-alpha #RGBA form often unsupported, mandatory hash, case-insensitive hex digits, reserved black/white canvas tones, alpha windows that exclude the degenerate 00 and FF bytes, strict-string validation posture), not from any WiseCounsil design document.
